title: Observability retention tiering and security questionnaire playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a combined pricing & contract playbook that treats observability retention (logs/traces/metrics audit logs) as a billable add-on and bundles a pre-populated security questionnaire response package (enterprise compliance pack) to accelerate sales cycles. Objective: validate pricing elasticity for retention windows (7/30/90/365 days), measure conversion uplift when providing pre-filled security questionnaire templates and legal-safe contract language for data retention, and define the gating UX + backend entitlements required to ship as an add-on in Hosted and Dedicated deployments.
updates: 2025-11-01 - Kickoff: scoped hypothesis and metrics (conversion rate, average contract TTV, MRR uplift, support overhead). Eng spike requested for retention metadata and billing dimensions.

2025-11-04 - Eng triage: ENG-4312 to add retention_period field to billing events; ENG-4379 to add entitlement flag for 'observability-retention-add-on'. Estimated 2 sprints for full backend plus billing ingestion changes.

2025-11-06 - Legal reviewed sample contract language; requested explicit deletion SLA and customer opt-in checkbox. Legal requires retention tiers to be represented in the contract appendix. Follow-up assigned to Legal and Sales Ops.

2025-11-08 - Design mockups (DES-56) of Console add-on purchase flow and per-route retention selector reviewed by PM/Eng. Decision: show forecasted monthly cost per GB for each tier and an estimated monthly spend slider.

2025-11-10 - Sales trial: created a 'fast response' security questionnaire template (SaaS vendor questionnaire) and a matching one-pager for CSMs to include in enterprise pitches. Initial feedback from Solutions Eng: templates reduce questionnaire turnaround by ~30% in pilot accounts.

2025-11-12 - Roadblock noted: SOC2 artifact generation and formal attestation cannot be auto-fulfilled; product will provide documentation and a templated answer pack but Sales must coordinate formal attestations. Added as constraint in playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Backend emits billing dimension 'retention_tier' and totals usage per retention tier into billing exports (CSV/BigQuery).
Console shows add-on purchase flow with 7/30/90/365 day options and clear cost estimate before checkout.
Pre-filled security questionnaire pack (PDF + CSV answers) generated for top 20 enterprise questionnaire sections and accessible from the contract workspace.
Sales toolkit (email templates + one-pager) included in the playbook and validated by Solutions Eng in at least 2 pilot deals.
Metrics dashboard tracks conversion from free -> paid for retention add-on, average MRR uplift, and support overhead per ticket type.
Security review completed and Legal-approved contract appendix templates added to the entitlements docs.
artifacts: GitHub: PR ENG-4312 add retention billing metadata: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427
decisions: Expose four retention tiers: 7d (free), 30d (starter add-on), 90d (standard add-on), 365d (premium add-on).

Charge per-GB-month for retention storage + flat per-account admin fee for premium SLA customers. Initial suggested pricing: $0.02/GB-month for 30d, $0.015/GB-month for 90d, $0.012/GB-month for 365d (discounted for committed contracts).
Include a templated security questionnaire pack as a sales enablement asset rather than a fully automated attestation.
Premium SLA will be offered as an upsell (99.9% uptime, priority support, 4-hour incident response) and requires legal sign-off for SLOs in contract appendix.
risks: Cost predictability: long-tail storage costs could erode margin if the pricing model is incorrect; need cost model stress tests.
Sales friction: multi-step questionnaire and attestation expectations may still delay deals despite templates.
Operational complexity: support and billing will need new flows (retention changes mid-cycle, retroactive refunds).
Compliance gap: some enterprise customers will require additional third-party attestations (SOC2/HIPAA) that we cannot auto-provide.
